dimensions.rationale: All interactive elements are native: skip links are <a>, search uses <input type='search'> with <label>, questions use native <details>/<summary>, phone uses <a href='tel:...'>, contact is <a>. No <dl> for FAQs. No div-soup for interactive controls. <section> used for FAQ categories appropriately.

Exactly one <h1> ('Frequently Asked Questions'). Four <h2> headings follow without skipping levels: 'Getting Started', 'Billing & Plans', 'Integrations', and 'Still need help?'. No levels are skipped and headings reflect document outline, not visual styling.

Skip links ('Skip to content' and 'Skip to search') are the first focusable elements. <main id='main-content'> wraps only FAQ content, outside <header> and <footer>. Breadcrumb <nav aria-label='Breadcrumb'> is correctly labelled. However, the primary site nav in <header> and the footer <nav> both lack aria-label/aria-labelledby, leaving multiple unlabelled <nav> landmarks that assistive technology cannot distinguish. The <search> landmark element was not used for the search input section.

ARIA usage is mostly disciplined: aria-current='page' on the breadcrumb current item is correct, and no redundant roles are applied. One issue: the search <input> carries both a <label for='search-input'> and aria-label='Search FAQ' with identical text — the aria-label redundantly overrides the already-correct <label>, which is unnecessary and slightly noisy.

summary: The output is strong overall: all key element choices are correct (details/summary for FAQ, tel: links, ol breadcrumb, no dl misuse), heading hierarchy is perfect, and skip links are present. Two dimensions are docked one point each: landmark_structure loses a point for unlabelled primary and footer navs (multiple nav elements need distinguishing aria-labels) and the absence of the <search> landmark; aria_discipline loses a point for a redundant aria-label on the search input that duplicates the already-correct <label> element.
